newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metal trade hit by slack demand, imports.
newsitem.headline: Indian metal trade hit by slack demand, imports.

text.p: Slow domestic demand and competition from imported semi-finished products reduced sales of Indian non-ferrous metals during the week, dealers said on Wednesday.

"LME (London Metals Exchange) prices are good but the local market is not picking up because of a money crunch in the non-ferrous sector," Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metal Exchange, told Reuters.
Parikh said several metal firms were cutting back production because they were unable to sell the finished products. Low industrial demand was also affecting the market, he said.
Traders said imports of finished goods were preferred because of the duty parity between raw materials and finished products. Also, credit facilities offered on imports were more attractive.
Parikh said the duty parity was affecting copper and zinc semis, mainly strips, cables, wire rods and tubes.
"Metal prices are steady, the market at the lower level is stable, but there is no demand," Parikh said.
He said state-run Hindustan Copper Limited (HCL) was likely to revise its prices upwards by at least two to three rupees per kg since LME prices were stable.
In the week to Wednesday, aluminium gained 4,250 rupees per tonne and copper gained 500 rupees while zinc was quoted 1,000 higher.
